comment: Compact STRICT-FAILURE shapes for the replay harness in
tests/test_strict_failure_replay.py. Each case is a complete, minimal payload
that reproduces one class of pre-export strict failure observed in the runs
and issue log, not a transcript of any single run: a real merged payload from
2026-07-28 is 306 KB in one leg and 4.7 MB in another, carries verbatim source
passages, and still would not say which field mattered.
The base pathway -- two-step glutathione biosynthesis with wrapped enzymes --
passes validate_required_pwml_contract(strict_db=True) on its own, so every
assertion below is attributable to the one defect the case adds.
'recovers' is the deliverable question: does pre-export quarantine turn this
strict failure into a SMALLER VALID strict graph, or does it correctly refuse?
Both answers are correct results. What is never correct is a graph that passes
because the pathway was emptied out, which is what cases 5 and 6 pin.

cases.title: An over-generated reaction whose participants were never declared
cases.observed_as: AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.md issue 5a -- jasmonate biosynthesis, 21 errors / 48 warnings
cases.why_it_matters: The LLM produced ~22 reactions for a ~9-step pathway. The surplus rows name participants no entity bucket carries, and the required-field gate fails the whole file over them. The nine good reactions were never written.

cases.title: A metabolite name split at its colon and filed as a protein complex
cases.why_it_matters: 'OPC-8:0-CoA' is a compound. Split at the colon it becomes a complex whose two components resolve to no declared protein, and it collides with the compound of the same name -- an entity-type overlap the closure must report rather than guess its way out of.

expect.strict_before_note: The current gate stack passes this: it forbids a proteins/protein_complexes overlap and nothing else, so a compound and a complex sharing a name goes unremarked and the IR resolves the reference to whichever was registered first.

cases.title: An enzyme no database resolves, wrapped and exported anyway
cases.why_it_matters: Plant enzymes with abbreviated gene symbols routinely resolve to nothing. Under strict export the wrapper component has no UniProt accession and the whole file fails; the two reactions that ARE fully mapped should still ship.

cases.title: A correctly formed Unknown-backed functional complex
cases.why_it_matters: This is the sanctioned representation of an enzyme the databases do not carry. Quarantining it for 'no real UniProt ID' would delete the exact biology the fallback exists to preserve, and would do it to every genuinely novel enzyme.

cases.title: Nothing survives quarantine
cases.observed_as: the degenerate end of the reaction-inflation class
cases.why_it_matters: An empty graph violates no gate, because there is nothing left to violate one. Strict success has to mean the pathway exported, not that nothing invalid remained.

cases.title: Every requested-core reaction is quarantined and an off-topic one is not
cases.observed_as: the failure mode a pure 'is anything left?' check cannot see
cases.why_it_matters: The survivor is complete, gate-clean and has nothing to do with the request. Coverage is measured against core-accepted processes only, so it scores zero and cannot carry the run.

expect.release_status_note: Since C-041a (4177fe5, under D-002) a minimum_core shortfall with a defensible surviving core is CLASSIFIED, not refused: ok is True and the graph is a smaller valid strict graph, while release.status is review_required and strict_acceptance_eligible is False. The off-topic survivor therefore still cannot read as a win -- the verdict moved from refusal_reasons to review_reasons, it did not disappear. F-142.

cases.title: A fully mapped protein with no edge in the graph
cases.observed_as: runs/2026-07-28_2122 PMC12444477 -- 'Protein has degree 0 after normalization: FabA'
cases.why_it_matters: Identity and connectivity are independent. FabA carried species and an accession and still failed, because the reactions named its partner instead. Closure drops it from the strict output; no process is touched.

cases.title: A production-valid coupled transport that the IR cannot emit
cases.observed_as: pwml/ir.py:1934-1946 builds every RCT with empty left/right/enzymes
cases.why_it_matters: This row is well formed by every schema in the repo and still cannot ship: build_pwml_ir hard-codes an RCT's left, right and enzymes to [] and never fills them, and validate_pwml_ir then raises rct_missing_left / _right / _enzyme for it. Admitting it would hand a reviewer a payload guaranteed to fail IR validation two stages later, so the refusal is explicit and named.

expect.strict_before_note: Neither the Stage 3 gate nor the required-field contract inspects reaction_coupled_transports; the failure is in the IR, further down.

cases.title: A transport keyed transport_elements and an interaction keyed left/right
cases.observed_as: the shapes pwml/ir.py:1780 and process_normalizer.py:4188 read first
cases.why_it_matters: The positive control. An admission rule that reads only `cargo` and only `entity_1`/`entity_2` records both of these as having no participants at all and quarantines them -- a false negative on the primary spelling of each. Nothing here may be touched.
